description: A `struct` type name colliding with a user procedure raises `ol-duplicate-definition` at phase-1 registration: `foo` is already declared on line 1, so `struct foo` cannot also register a constructor of that name. Issue #839 moved this off `ol-reserved-word{namespace:"procedure"}` — ruling #833 rule 6 gives a name the LEARNER already declared its own code, distinct from `ol-reserved-word`'s "OpenLogo owns this name". The two declarations differ in KIND (`define` then `struct`), which is the cross-kind half of `spec/error-model.md:126` ("a procedure and a struct with the same name in either order"); `data/check/duplicate-definition-across-declaration-slots` pins the same program at check stage, and `params.original_span` proves the runtime shares the checker's one first-declaration map rather than keeping a separate one per kind.

diagnostics.message: you already defined foo on line 1.
